lesson_title: You Are Standing on a Giant Magnet
hook_text: Deep under your feet, swirling liquid iron is making the planet a magnet. Your compass knows.
clip_script: Grab two magnets. North and north: they shove each other away. North and south: they snap together. Like poles repel, unlike poles attract. Magnets are fussy, too. They grab iron, nickel, cobalt and steel, but ignore aluminium, copper and gold. Snap a magnet in half and you do not get a lone north and a lone south; you get two new magnets. Now zoom out. The whole Earth is a magnet. Swirling molten iron in the core makes a field that wraps around the planet. A compass is just a tiny magnet that swings to line up with it, which is how sailors crossed oceans. That same field is a shield, pushing away the stream of charged particles from the Sun. The few that sneak in near the poles light up the sky as the southern and northern lights. Turtles and birds use the field as a map.
visual_style: Two magnets snapping and repelling; iron filings forming field lines; a cutaway Earth with a glowing core and a bar magnet overlay; aurora over Antarctica.
pacing: Quick hands-on start, a zoom out to space, then a slow aurora finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and map a magnetic field with iron filings.
